Definition: Percentage of individuals who used the internet (from any location, via any device) in the last three months. This measures actual internet adoption beyond network availability, capturing the combined effect of infrastructure, affordability, digital literacy, and relevance.
revision_notes: Cited sources checked. DataReportal (Digital 2023: Benin) confirms 4.60 million internet users at start of 2023, an internet penetration rate of 34.0% of the total population. This falls within the 30-49% band, supporting the existing Value Code of 3. World Bank ITU-sourced indicator page for Benin (IT.NET.USER.ZS) is consistent but the live figure is not directly extractable from the dynamic page. Score confirmed unchanged.
revised_comments: An estimated 34.0% of Benin's population used the internet in early 2023, equivalent to around 4.6 million internet users out of a population of 13.5 million, according to DataReportal's Digital 2023: Benin report drawing on Kepios analysis. This places internet usage in the 30-49% band.

Definition: The gap between urban and rural electricity access rates. A smaller gap indicates more equitable energy distribution, critical for ensuring ICT infrastructure can serve the whole population, not just cities.
revision_notes: Original source (a 2020 World Bank BEAS project appraisal PDF) was fetched and read; it does not itself contain a stated urban/rural electrification gap figure in its opening pages, and the cited 73%/17%/56pp figures in the original Comments were not verified in the document text retrieved. Even taking the original comment's own figures at face value (56pp), this falls in the 41-60pp band (Value Code 2 under the metadata scale), not the >60pp band (Value Code 1) that was recorded - the original scoring was inconsistent with its own cited evidence. Fresher and more directly sourced World Bank Open Data (indicators EG.ELC.ACCS.UR.ZS and EG.ELC.ACCS.RU.ZS, as reproduced by CountryDataHub and Trading Economics) show, for 2023, urban electricity access of 70.3% and rural access of 43.7%, a gap of 26.6 percentage points. This falls within the 21-40pp band. Score recalculated to 3.
revised_comments: Benin's electrification gap between urban and rural areas has narrowed considerably in recent years. World Bank Open Data indicators put urban electricity access at 70.3% and rural access at 43.7% in 2023, a gap of 26.6 percentage points, reflecting continued investment in rural electrification, including the World Bank-financed Benin Electricity Access Scale-up (BEAS) Project.
